#define ucl_chunk_skipc(chunk, p)    \
do {                                 \
        if (*(p) == '\n') {          \
                (chunk)->line ++;    \
                (chunk)->column = 0; \
        }                            \
        else (chunk)->column ++;     \
        (p++);                       \
        (chunk)->pos ++;             \
        (chunk)->remain --;          \
} while (0)

static inline void

message.content:
I see! The macro does `(p++)` which increments `p` (the local pointer). After skipping the backslash, `p` is incremented. If the string ends with `\`, then `p` was pointing to the last byte (the `\`), and after increment, `p` points to `chunk->begin + size = chunk->end`.

But wait - the macro also does `if (*(p) == '\n')` BEFORE incrementing `p`. So when `p` points to the backslash, `*(p)` is `\\` (0x5c), not `\n`, so it just does `(p++)`. Now `p = chunk->end`.

Then `c = *p;` reads from `chunk->end`, which is one byte past the buffer. This should be caught by ASAN.

Let me check if maybe the issue is that `ucl_parser_add_string` with `len != 0` goes through a different path. Let me look at `ucl_parser_add_chunk_full` again - it stores `chunk->begin = data` and `chunk->end = data + len`. But maybe the data gets copied somewhere?
